newsitem.title: UK: IBCA AFFIRMS HSB'S CLAIMS SETTLING ABILITY RATING.
newsitem.headline: IBCA AFFIRMS HSB'S CLAIMS SETTLING ABILITY RATING.

text.p: LONDON, June 10 - IBCA, the European credit rating agency, has affirmed its Claims Settling Ability rating of AA (Excellent security) assigned to HSB Engineering Insurance Limited (HSB) based in London.
HSB is a specialist engineering risk insurer writing an international portfolio of risks for industries that are heavily dependent on plant and machinery.

The rating reflects the company's excellent earnings, good capitalisation and high quality of underwriting and management. It is owned by the Hartford Steam Boiler Inspection and Insurance Company Inc.
HSB is responsible for all group insurance operations outside North America and currently trades in over 60 countries.
Core business is the provision of Machinery Breakdown, Erection All Risks and Business Interruption cover. Key sectors are power generation, pulp & paper, cement and heavy manufacturing.
The company enjoyed buoyant growth in 1996 and started a new line of schemes aimed at large volume, small ticket commercial business under the "HSB Affinity" brand.

HSB's concept of operations is to apply engineering and technology to design risk management and loss prevention programmes. This is reflected in above average operating costs, but is mitigated by a lower claims ratio.

The combined ratio of 93.1% achieved in 1996 was above target, but was still a creditable result. The company is well-capitalised. Although the solvency margin ratio of 182.3% was lower, due to the rapid growth of Net Premium Written, in IBCA's opinion it remains strong and provides adequate capacity for foreseeable growth.
Technical reserves are considered satisfactory. The company has had a year of buoyant, but disciplined growth.
The reinsurance programme protects it from high losses arising from either a single claim or an accumulation of smaller claims.

Underwriting continued to produce an impressive combined ratio indicating firm control of pricing, risk selection and loss prevention. However, technical earnings appear to be under growing pressure and the effect of attempts to diversify the revenue stream is yet to make itself known.
HSB's liquidity is influenced to a degree by the flow of dividends from its subsidiary The Boiler Inspection and Insurance Company of Canada which to date has been profitable.
Nevertheless, in our opinion the company is well-resourced and managed, capitalisation is good and policyholders are well-protected.
